title: C918 inline connector reference
introduction:
This inline connector brings together lighting, microphone, communication, indicator and ground circuits. Think of the housing as a shared apartment building: neighboring cavities can belong to entirely different electrical households.

I start with the harness heading, then use that face’s drawing to find a cavity label and read across its table. Cavity identifies the position; Circuit Number and Function identify the electrical job. Read Color, Gauge, Qualifier, Used and Terminal Part Number from that same row. Colors can differ between the connector halves, and repeated cavity entries must stay separate when their configuration is unresolved.

The drawings reverse the left-to-right placement of the numbered banks. Their labels and housing outlines provide page landmarks, but the physical terminal-side or wire-side viewing direction is unspecified. Grey shading is a visual distinction; consult the associated row without assuming the shading means an absent circuit. Gauge conventions, Size and Used codes, and unexplained symbols remain literal reference data. This page supports reading the connector record; physical access, release movements, probing, test limits and replacement selection require separate instructions.

The summary Pin Count disagrees with the numbered positions in both drawings and the pigtail cavity count. That count discrepancy remains unresolved; it does not establish an additional physical position.

edits.why: In this drawing, the lower-numbered bank is on the left. I use the printed labels and housing outline to locate a position on the page. The housing projections do not establish how to release or disconnect the connector.

Read each cavity across its complete row. The functions distinguish fuse-or-circuit-breaker supplies, lighting controls, microphone connections, indicator connections, battery-saver relay circuitry, LIN communication and ground. Microphone polarity marks belong to their named circuits; they do not independently identify a chassis ground. LIN identifies a local message link. Repeated microphone-return entries have different color descriptions and no qualifier selecting between them.

The lower-numbered bank is on the right in this drawing. I find the printed cavity label afresh when changing faces, because carrying a left-hand position straight across would land in the opposite bank. The heading identifies the harness association without establishing a physical viewing direction.

Use this face’s rows for its colors, gauges and terminal references; matching circuit identities can have different descriptions across the halves. Some cavity labels have both convertible-roof-switch and ambient-noise-microphone entries with blank qualifiers. Keep those entries distinct: this reference does not select their vehicle configuration or establish that both functions occupy the position together. Retain the fuse-or-circuit-breaker protection alternatives.

Keep each kit’s service part, engineering shell, material, gauge and cavity-count fields together as its own catalog entry. The two rows list different shells and materials; neither row establishes interchangeability or selects replacement wire. Tin (greased) is the listed material description, not an instruction to apply grease. Pigtail installation requires separate service information.

originalAuthorHold: The metadata Pin Count exceeds the numbered cavity positions shown in both face illustrations. The supplied values remain unchanged; the meaning of that count needs reconciliation.

editorialRevision.scope: Complete independent active-agent review of all 70 primary units, four complete source pages and both figures, and all 5 edits. Original first CLI author covered 60 units and only 4 headings. Complete draft adds pigtail heading and explanation, retains explicit female 4 and 5 assignment conflicts and summary 17 versus 16 cavity-count uncertainty, and covers remaining female rows, pigtail table and raw tail. Original partial author retained separately. Physical assignments remain unresolved for bounded source reading only.
